entry.title: Heat-related deaths in Phoenix rise, after two years of decline
entry.summary: Metro Phoenix has so far seen twice as many heat deaths as this time last year. Authorities are trying to understand why and how to intervene.

entry.title: 'It's a nightmare.' Former refugee, professor on Trump's new Medicaid policy
entry.summary: Starting Oct. 1, many immigrants who are here legally lose their Medicaid coverage because of the Republican budget bill passed last year.

entry.title: A new California law bans child marriage. What's the global outlook on the practice?
entry.summary: The governor of California has signed into law a ban on child marriage. What is the status of other efforts to ban the practice? And do bans prove effective?

entry.title: Trump administration reverses stance on integration of people with disabilities
entry.summary: Disability rights advocates are angered by the latest reversal but are rallying behind proposed legislation and working with states to strengthen protections for community integration.

entry.title: After failed execution, health workers say Tennessee's method flouts medical ethics
entry.summary: After a botched lethal injection in May, dozens of Tennessee medical professionals told the governor that healthcare professionals shouldn't help with executions, no matter the method.

entry.title: Travel plans? Here's what to know as measles exposures reach trains and games
entry.summary: Measles is traveling, with outbreaks in Pennsylvania, Ohio and New York, and exposures on transportation and in sports. What should you know before getting on a plane or train?

entry.title: What's behind HHS claims that gender-affirming care 'may' radicalize
entry.summary: The report is the agency's latest effort to chip away at trust in established health care models for transgender people. Critics say it frames transgender identity as illegitimate or even dangerous.

entry.title: Montana starts enforcing Medicaid work requirements on Oct 1. Patients are confused
entry.summary: In most states, people with Medicaid coverage will have to prove they're working, volunteering or studying, starting Jan. 1. But Montana is starting that early, and it's sowing confusion and anxiety.

entry.title: They were promised protection. Instead, these kids with disabilities died in foster care
entry.summary: Disabled kids make up the largest group in foster care. They have the worst outcomes. They stay in foster care longest. They're the most likely to die.

entry.title: Drugs are widely used to sedate dementia patients. Her sons wanted to keep her off them
entry.summary: Potent sedating medications are often used on agitated people with dementia in long-term care facilities despite federal efforts to discourage them. A clash over whether to drug a Michigan woman illuminates the wrenching decisions families and guardians face.
